vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability exists in the launchRestrict modifier when state == State.Restricted. It updates lastTx for both sender and recipient to block.timestamp, then requires that lastTx[sender].add(60) <= block.timestamp and lastTx[recipient].add(60) <= block.timestamp. This means after a transfer, both parties cannot make another transaction for 60 seconds. An attacker can exploit this by sending tiny amounts (1 wei) to multiple victim addresses, locking each victim out of transactions for 60 seconds. Since the attacker controls when to send, they can continuously lock victims out, creating a DoS.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to enable bot protection (set state to Restricted). 2. Get some BNRG tokens to the attacker address. 3. Create multiple victim addresses. 4. Transfer 1 wei of BNRG to each victim address, which will set their lastTx to current timestamp. 5. Verify that victims cannot transfer tokens for 60 seconds by attempting a transfer that should revert.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner and call setBotProtection(true) to enable Restricted mode. 2. Use deal() to give attacker BNRG tokens (need to find the correct storage slot for balances). 3. Create victim addresses using makeAddr(). 4. For each victim, transfer 1 wei of BNRG to them. 5. Immediately try to make a transfer from victim address (should revert due to lastTx check). 6. Use assert to verify the revert occurs.
